subject: ventures/tile-layout-planner
professional: a tile setter / flooring estimator who lays out rooms and orders tile, grout and thinset (TCNA Handbook and ANSI A108 practice)

evidence.correctness: Ran a script (scratchpad a.mjs) importing calc.mjs and compared with hand arithmetic. (1) 3000x2000 room, 300 mm tile, 3 mm joint, corner start, no obstacles: pitch 303, 9 full columns (9*303+300<=3000), 6 full rows, so 54 full, cuts 9+6+1=16, 70 tiles, order ceil(70*1.1)=77, smallest cut 182 mm (=2000-6*303). Tool: full 54, cutCount 16, tilesNoReuse 70, orderTiles 77, smallest 182. (2) 1000x1000, 500 mm tile, no joint, tile centred: 1 full, 8 cuts of >=250 mm; with reuse 1 + 2 (edge halves) + 1 (four quarters) = 4 = area/tile area. Tool: 1 full, 8 cuts, smallest 250, reuse 4. (3) 2000x2000, 500 tile, 750x750 cut-out in a corner: 12 full, 3 cut, tiled area 4-0.5625=3.4375 m2. Tool: 12/3, visible 3.4375 = tileableArea. (4) Diagonal 1 m square, 500 tile centred: 1 full + 4 + 4 cuts = 9, tool 9. (5) Joint volume for case 1, hand: visible = 54*90000+6*273*300+9*300*182+273*182 = 5,892,486 mm2, joint 107,514 mm2, x10 mm = 1.075 L, x1.86 = 2.00 kg; tool groutKg 1.99976. Rule-of-thumb TCNA-style grout formula (L+W)/(L*W)*J*T gives 0.2 L/m2 = 1.2 L for 6 m2, consistent with the exact 1.08 L (difference is the partial edge tiles). Thinset 6 m2 * 3.8 = 22.8 kg matches tool; 3.8 kg/m2 for a 1/4x3/8 notch is inside the 3.0-3.7 (50 lb per 60-75 ft2) manufacturer range, slightly high. Also verifyLayout returned [] for every case. No wrong number found; the layout engine is not checked against another tool, only hand cases.
evidence.completeness: README features checked: exact polygon clipping of tiles vs floor and cut-outs (works, cases above); straight / running bond / diagonal (sampleSpec brick best run: 19 full, 19 cuts, 25 tiles, 0 slivers, verify []); starting-position search with swap (searchBest, test 13); offcut reuse (works, C2 reuse 4); comparison of corner/centred/best (compareLayouts exists, tested in calc.test); cut list + CSV download button present (index.html:138); tiles and boxes to order (boxes 8 for 77 tiles at 10/box); metric and imperial (SYSTEMS); share link button (index.html:122) and localStorage; usage.mjs counters with Do Not Track opt-out; guide page with worked example (page.test.mjs test 34 passes); materials() grout/thinset (works); deploy files (Dockerfile, fly.toml, render.yaml; README itself says the image was never built). No stubs or TODOs found. I did not load the page in a browser; page behaviour was checked through page.test.mjs and by reading the module script only.
evidence.verification: Ran: cd ventures/tile-layout-planner && node --test '*.test.mjs' -> 44 tests, 44 pass, 0 fail. Seeded mutation 1 (calc.mjs evaluateLayout cut thickness Math.min -> Math.max of bbox sides): 5 tests failed (hand-computed 3000x2000, 2500 wide strips, centring, search without thin cuts, guide worked example). Seeded mutation 2 (grout density constant GROUT_KG_PER_L -> 1.6 in materials): 1 failure (materials test 19). Both reverted by restoring a saved copy; git status of the directory is clean. Weak spots: only 21 tests in calc.test.mjs, tests are mostly the author's own hand cases (several of which I re-derived and found right); the sliver boundary (< minCut - 1e-6) and the overage rounding were not mutated.
evidence.craft: Read calc.mjs (all ~580 lines), usage.mjs, test files. Pure ES module with no dependencies, millimetres internally, tolerance constants, validateSpec with specific messages and a MAX_CELLS guard, an independent verifyLayout that re-sums piece areas, a quick path for whole tiles. Defects: evaluateLayout is a ~110-line function mixing lattice maths, clipping and reporting; reuseTiles is greedy with no stated bound on how far from optimal; verifyLayout for non-zero grout only checks the area to within a perimeter-wide band (weak); the cut for a tile split into several pieces by an obstacle uses the combined bounding box, which is conservative but undocumented in the UI; index.html is a 42 kB single page with inline script (acceptable for a static tool).
evidence.claims: Checked against files: 'browser only, nothing uploaded' (no fetch in calc.mjs/usage.mjs, usage stored in localStorage, page.test) backed; no-warranty text and not-modelled list present in README and index.html:154,181 (blade width, breakage, herringbone, trims): backed; grout/thinset constants stated with limits and 'use your bag coverage': backed; 'tested on hand-computed layouts and random rooms': backed by tests. Not backed: llms.txt links to https://duncan-haywood.github.io/oss-monorepo/tile-layout-planner/ while the live address per README and repo policy is https://marisstella.app/tile-layout-planner/ (old Pages host now only redirects); sitemap.xml lists relative locs ('./index.html') and robots.txt gives 'Sitemap: ./sitemap.xml', which crawlers reject (sitemaps need absolute URLs), and canonical is './index.html', so the SEO files do nothing; the guide's 'the planner counts them exactly' for diagonal is true for geometry but the 'diagonal figure is conservative' claim has no test. The thinset figures are called 'typical' without a source citation. Docker/Fly/Render 'host your own' is flagged as untested in the README (honest).
evidence.fitness: Walked a bathroom job: 2.74 x 2.13 m with a tub cut-out, 300x600 tile, brick bond: sampleSpec best found 25 tiles to buy, 0 slivers, with a cut list, CSV and to-scale plan, which is the answer an installer needs. It handles cut-outs, wall gap, minimum cut, overage, box size and price, and the comparison table to justify a start line. Gaps a setter would hit: no blade kerf, no doorway or threshold, only rectangular cut-outs (no L-shaped rooms, so a real L or T room must be approximated by obstacles), no herringbone. These are stated, so the tool is usable with limits rather than misleading.
evidence.domain: Compared with practice in the TCNA Handbook and standard setting practice: centring or balancing the layout so edge cuts are not slivers, a minimum cut around 50 mm, running bond offset for rectangular tile (the page repeats the common 1/3 offset warning for long tiles; TCNA/ANSI A137.1 limits warpage-related offset on tile over 15 in, so 50% is not allowed by many makers: the tool allows it but tells the user to check), about 10% overage for straight and more for diagonal (page text agrees), the TCNA grout-quantity formula is matched by the exact method, and thinset coverage by notch is within published bag coverage ranges. Departures: default wall gap is 0 whereas TCNA EJ171 / perimeter movement joints call for a gap at walls (the input exists, not defaulted or mentioned prominently); no kerf; greedy offcut reuse is optimistic compared with real breakage (acknowledged); diagonal overage is not defaulted higher.

defects.what: sitemap.xml, robots.txt Sitemap line and the canonical link use relative URLs ('./index.html'), which search engines ignore or reject, so the page's SEO files do nothing
llms.txt points at the retired github.io host instead of https://marisstella.app/tile-layout-planner/
Default wall gap is 0 mm and perimeter movement joints (TCNA EJ171) are not mentioned as a reason to set it; a floor planned at 0 gap can under-count cuts at the walls
Only rectangular rooms: an L-shaped room has to be faked with obstacles; not listed under the not-modelled text
Thinset 3.8 kg/m2 for 1/4 x 3/8 notch is at the high end of manufacturer coverage charts and is uncited
Mutation coverage thin: sliver boundary and overage rounding are not pinned by a test that I could confirm; evaluateLayout is one 110-line function

verdict: A small, honest static tool whose core numbers I could reproduce by hand: five independent layout cases (full/cut counts, reuse, obstacle area, diagonal) and the exact grout volume all matched, 44 of 44 tests pass, and two seeded mutations were caught (5 and 1 failures). A tile setter could plan a room with it and the limits are written down. The weakest part is the surrounding distribution files: the sitemap, robots and canonical use relative URLs and llms.txt names a retired host, so the claims dimension scores 2 and the subject does not meet the bar by the computed rule (claims < 3), although it is finished (completeness 3). Rectangular-only rooms and a zero default wall gap are the practical limits a professional would hit first. The page was not loaded in a browser in this audit.
